page: OVHcloud c3-64 is a compute-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. The configuration features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance profiles across multiple compute and memory metrics. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 63662.12 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 98610.77, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with a Passmark memory score of 2995.4 placing in the top 10% tier, supported by a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 227.99 GB/sec. For database workloads, the server processed 77.38 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 31841.07 in Passmark database operations.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the c3-64 is characterized by its high compute-to-RAM density and dedicated core allocation, which eliminates resource contention. However, a potential tradeoff is the lack of hyperthreading and a relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which may limit memory-intensive applications. The server is suited for CPU-bound workloads, multi-threaded decompression tasks, database operations, and small-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its prompt processing speed of 2858.15 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.
